If the compiler-tree witness search is genuinely unbounded/stuck on this checkpoint+grammar, decode_outcome stays runtime_timeout regardless of how far the wall is pushed.

pattern.description: Across 4 trials spanning 2 distinct held_out records and 3 distinct decode-timeout-seconds values (30/60/90), every single trial ends in decode_outcome=runtime_timeout with latency_ms pinned almost exactly at the configured wall (offset by ~0-200ms of teardown, never less). There is no partial progress signal: no trial produced model_valid, model_invalid, fallback_output, or any latency meaningfully short of the wall. Tripling the wall (30s->90s) on the same record produced the identical outcome with the identical shape (pinned latency), not a shrinking gap toward completion.
pattern.verdict: The compiler-tree witness search for these held_out records does not exhibit convergent behavior as wall-clock budget grows within the tested range. This is evidence of a genuinely unbounded/stuck search for this checkpoint+grammar combination on these records, not a timeout that is merely a little short. A defensible eval-config change (e.g. bumping the production default to 60s or 90s) would require seeing decode outcomes start flipping to real completions as the wall grows; that was not observed at any tested point.

budget_constraint_note: MAX_RUN_MINUTES=3 (170s harness-interrupt budget) bounds each invocation. Each trial here was --eval-limit 1 (single record) so even the 90s trial fit in ~103s wall-clock, leaving margin. A full 5-record held_out suite at 90s/record (450s worst case) would blow the cap in one invocation, which is why this diagnostic used isolated single-record probes as instructed rather than a full-suite longer-wall run.

ship_gate_check.reason: n=1 per trial, diagnostic isolation slices -- not a scoreboard claim; no --ship-gates flag used

decision: INCONCLUSIVE-TOWARD-NOWHERE-CLOSE: within the tested budget (30/60/90s, 2 records), the 30s wall shows no sign of being merely miscalibrated. Every trial pins exactly at whatever wall is configured, with zero partial-progress or near-miss signal. This is the stronger, more serious finding named in the task: evidence for a genuinely unbounded/stuck compiler-tree witness search on this checkpoint+grammar, not a wall that just needs a modest honest bump.
